why: One executor's `/diagnostics` publisher and its sent/failed counters; the violation sink maps each violation through `nros-diagnostics`' `report_violation`. issue 1676 -- `nros::contract`, the on-target half of RFC-0052's contract monitors that a Rust entry reaches: `nros::main!` installs the baked tables through it, and nros-cpp's `nros_cpp_install_monitors` arms the same reporter. No rclrs counterpart -- ROS 2 has no contract monitors; the observer reads the reports on `/diagnostics` in play_launch's RFC-0050 rule vocabulary. See `rust:MonitorSpec`.
